<!--
  CHAPTER TEMPLATE — integrated_bioanalytics
  ============================================
  This is the canonical skeleton for a chapter of the book. To add a chapter:

    1. Copy this file to chapters/<N>_<short_name>.Rmd  (e.g. 19_networks.Rmd)
    2. Fill in the sections below and delete these guiding comments.
    3. Register it in ../index.Rmd with a child chunk, in reading order:
         ```{r child="chapters/<N>_<short_name>.Rmd"}
         ```
       (Chapters are merged via explicit child= chunks, NOT auto-collected.)
    4. Re-render.

  Files whose names begin with "_" are not rendered, so this template never
  appears in the book.

  Standard structure — keep this order (see any existing chapter for a live example):
    1. Chapter heading            # title {-}
    2. Opening image              HTML-only include_graphics chunk
    3. Preamble                   two sentences: "X uses the concept of Y to do Z to a dataset"
                                  (naming every method), then "This analysis can be used to answer
                                  questions such as '...?' or '...?'" (questions the analysis itself
                                  answers)
    4. Separator                  ## {-}
    5. Opening paragraph          a few sentences: what questions these methods answer and where
                                  they are used, so the reader knows why before how
    6. Separator                  ## {-}
    7. Content sections           ## section {-}  /  ### subsection {-}
    8. Separator                  ## {-}  (the TOC gap before the closing trio)
    9. Chapter summary            ## chapter summary {-}, then the {.summary-pdf} link to
                                  summary_sheets/<file stem>.pdf (shown on the heading's line), then
                                  a ::: {.summary-top} div holding flowchart + recap (two columns in
                                  HTML), then the function table (small text)
   10. <hr>
   11. Exercises                  ## exercises {-}  (usually commented out)
   12. <hr>                       (an <hr>, not ## {-}: summary, exercises and further reading
                                  sit together in the TOC)
   13. Further reading            ## further reading {-}  (3–5 annotated links)

  Conventions:
    - The {-} after every heading suppresses bookdown's automatic numbering.
    - Cite with [@bibkey]; keys live in ../book.bib, rendered with
      chicago-fullnote-bibliography.csl.
    - Default chunk options come from ../_common.R and index.Rmd; only set
      per-chunk options (fig.width, out.width, message, etc.) when needed.
-->
